title: Understanding sex differences in long-term outcomes after a first episode of psychosis
cohort_overlap_notes: Same PAFIP cohort as mayoralvanson2019 (Programa Asistencial Fases Iniciales de Psicosis, Marques de Valdecilla University Hospital, Santander, Cantabria). This report describes PAFIP-10: 307 patients referred February 2001 to December 2008 with baseline measures, 209 reassessed 8 to 16 years later. mayoralvanson2019 analyses 'a subsample of 157 patients within PAFIP' whose relation to these 307 is never stated, so the two analysed samples overlap by an unknown amount.
notes: ELIGIBILITY CHANGED from the manifest's linked_report to include with report_quantifiable = no, under D10.2. linked_report means the result used comes from another report of the same cohort, and no other PAFIP report supplies the 8-to-16-year horizon this report covers: the loss is a numerator/denominator loss and must stay visible at that gate. WHY UNQUANTIFIABLE: Table 1 reports 'Unemployed (yes)' and 'Student (yes)' only, by sex. At the 10-year reassessment the denominators are NOT printed; they are recoverable only by dividing the printed count by the printed percentage (35/0.327 = 107 male, 22/0.244 = 90 female), which is a back-calculation from a percentage and is forbidden. Baseline denominators ARE printed (N = 114 male, N = 95 female) so baseline employed is recoverable by complement (114-54 = 60 male, 95-27 = 68 female), but baseline is not a follow-up timepoint. No employment result at 12 months or later can be extracted from this report.

title: Unemployment, Homelessness, and Other Societal Outcomes Among US Veterans With Schizophrenia Relapse: A Retrospective Cohort Study
journal: The Primary Care Companion For CNS Disorders
cohort_overlap_notes: COHORT CONFIRMED us_vha, same source cohort as lin2022. Figure 1 of this report and Figure 1 of lin2022 print the identical patient-selection cascade from the same database and the same study period: 132,153 with two or more schizophrenia diagnoses (1 Jan 2013 to 30 Sep 2019); 127,366 with one in the selection window (1 Jan 2014 to 30 Sep 2019); 125,595 enrolled in VA benefits for 12 months pre-index; 119,601 with a benefit record pre- and post-index; and an overall schizophrenia cohort of 119,343. Both cite the same Veterans Affairs Central IRB approval (1478231-1, 17 December 2019) and this report calls lin2022 'An early phase of this study' (Discussion). The analysed samples differ: lin2022 propensity-matches 102,207 of the 119,343 to non-schizophrenia veterans, this report splits the same 119,343 into a relapse cohort (16,866) and a nonrelapse cohort (102,477) and propensity-matches 16,862 from each. Participants overlap heavily; the two reports are not independent samples.
notes: AUTHORSHIP: the article of record prints Benson C first and Lin D second, while Crossref, PubMed and the article's own 'To cite' line list Lin D first; report_id follows the article of record, as the manifest already decided. PDF is a print of the publisher's free full text with the five figure and table GIFs appended as pages 3 to 7 (Tables 1-3, then Figures 1-2); all five were legible and were read for this extraction.

title: Unemployment, homelessness, and other societal outcomes in patients with schizophrenia: a real-world retrospective cohort study of the United States Veterans Health Administration database
cohort_overlap_notes: Same us_vha source cohort as benson2022; see benson2022's cohort_overlap_notes for the identical selection cascade. This report's analysed sample is the 102,207 schizophrenia veterans propensity-matched to non-schizophrenia veterans.
notes: WHY UNQUANTIFIABLE: the only labour-market measure is UNEMPLOYMENT, reported as a percentage in a bar chart (Figure 2a, 69.2 per cent for the schizophrenia cohort) with no count and no stated denominator. Employment is not the complement of unemployment here: the sibling report benson2022 uses the same Veterans Benefits Administration employment field and shows it has six categories (full-time, part-time, unemployed, retired, self-employed, missing), with 15.8 per cent retired and 3.3 per cent missing in a cohort of the same median age. Subtracting 69.2 per cent from 100 would count retired and missing veterans as employed. No employment numerator or denominator is recoverable without back-calculation, so no result row is written.
